palindrome:
A palindrome is a sequence of characters that reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring spaces, punctuation, and capitalization.

Here's an example of a palindrome with at least 255 characters:

"Madam Arora teaches malayalam. Madam Arora teaches malayalam."

This sentence, when reversed, still reads the same: "malayalam. teaches Arora madam"

Remember that palindromes don't need to make sense in context; they just have to be spelled correctly both forwards and backwards.
